filters.name: Parametrize by Voronoi Atlas (vcglib)
filters.shortDescription: Build an atlased parametrization using a geodesic Voronoi partition of the surface.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Build an atlased parametrization based on a geodesic voronoi partitioning of the surface and parametrizing each region using Harmonic Mapping. The harmonic map of each disk-like region is that of Pinkall and Polthier.

parameters.label: Approx. Region Num
parameters.help: An estimation of the number of regions that must be generated. Smaller regions could lead to parametrizations with smaller distortion.

parameters.label: Overlap
parameters.help: If checked the resulting parametrization will be composed by overlapping regions, e.g. the resulting mesh will have duplicated faces: each region will have a ring of ovelapping duplicate faces that will ensure that border regions will be parametrized in the atlas twice. This is quite useful for building mipmap robust atlases.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Zero draws a fresh seed on every run, so repeated applications differ; any other value makes the atlas regions exactly reproducible.

filters.name: Parametrize Surface along Polyline (Local Flattening)
filters.shortDescription: Create a rectangular patch of the surface around a polyline, flattened with proportional UVs in the unit square.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Flatten a strip of the current surface that runs along a polyline drawn on it, into a rectangle: the local flattening operator of Pietroni et al., which turns a portion of a scanned artwork into an image in which lengths can be measured, carved marks compared and photographs laid side by side.

The faces within a geodesic distance of the polyline a little over the half-width are taken, and must form a disk. A conformal map that pulls the polyline onto a straight line gives a cross field that follows it, and the strip is then parametrized aligned to that field. The result is cropped exactly to the rectangle $2w \times L$, the polyline running along its middle in the $V$ direction from its end with the lower index, where $w$ is the half-width and $L$ the polyline's straightened length.

The patch is a **new layer** with per-vertex and per-wedge texture coordinates scaled uniformly into the unit square, its longer side spanning 0 to 1, so texture tools can use it at once: lengths in UV are lengths on the surface divided by `uv_scale`, an output value. The current mesh is left unchanged. *Remesh as a grid* replaces the surface's own triangles with a regular grid over the rectangle, meshed in parametric space; *Smoothing* keeps only the patch's overall shape, moving each point along the normal, as the paper does with its geometry image. To make a height map of the residual marks, smooth the patch, then bake the original surface onto it with *Transfer Vertex Attributes from Another Layer to Texture*, *Signed Distance* and *Along the normal*; photographs go onto it with *Transfer Color from Visible Rasters to Texture*. The log and the output values report the distortion as the paper does: the smallest and largest ratio between an edge's length on the surface and in UV, and their average deviation from 1. They also count the faces folded in UV (`folded_faces`), which should be none: a fold marks a triangle turned back onto its neighbour in the surface, which no flat map can lay out (*Select Ill-Shaped Faces* finds them), or a region too curved for the half-width.

The paper's equation 1 pulls only the U coordinate of the polyline to a constant. Here V is also pulled to the arc length along the polyline, which on a developable surface cuts the length distortion by an order of magnitude; the polyline need not be a geodesic, and is straightened. The polyline must be a single open curve lying on the surface, and is assumed to be smooth: its points are pulled onto a straight line and its arc length becomes length in the patch, so a zigzag would be straightened into a distorted patch. The edge paths *Create Polyline from Geodesic Path* makes zigzag along mesh edges; smooth them first with *Smooth Polyline on Surface*.

parameters.label: Polyline
parameters.help: The polyline layer the patch runs along: a single open curve lying on the current mesh. It is left unchanged.

parameters.label: Half-width
parameters.help: Half the width of the patch, measured on the surface from the polyline to each long side of the rectangle.

parameters.label: Remesh as a grid
parameters.help: If above zero, the patch is remeshed in parametric space as a regular grid of this step, laid exactly on the rectangle, instead of keeping the surface's own triangles. Nodes take the color, scalar and normal of the surface under them; holes stay holes.

parameters.label: Smoothing (sigma)
parameters.help: If above zero, the patch's shape is smoothed by a Gaussian of this standard deviation, moving each point only along the normal: the smooth base whose normals the detail can then be projected along. Features much narrower than sigma are removed.

parameters.label: Alignment stiffness
parameters.help: How strongly the polyline is pulled onto the straight V axis when the cross field is computed (k_st in the paper). Higher values follow the polyline more closely.

filters.name: Convert Per-Wedge UV to Per-Vertex UV
filters.shortDescription: Convert per-wedge texture coordinates into per-vertex texture coordinates, splitting vertices when needed.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Converts per Wedge Texture Coordinates to per Vertex Texture Coordinates splitting vertices with not coherent Wedge coordinates.

filters.name: Convert Per-Vertex UV to Per-Wedge UV
filters.shortDescription: Convert per-vertex texture coordinates into per-wedge texture coordinates.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Converts per Vertex Texture Coordinates to per Wedge Texture Coordinates. It does not merge superfluous vertices...

parameters.label: Projection plane
parameters.help: Choose the projection plane.

parameters.label: Preserve Ratio
parameters.help: If checked the resulting parametrization will preserve the original apsect ratio of the model otherwise it will fill up the whole 0..1 uv space.

parameters.label: Side Gutter
parameters.help: Leave an empty space around the parametrization area of the specified size (in texture space); accepted range [0.0 - 0.5].

filters.name: Parametrize by Trivial Per-Triangle Layout
filters.shortDescription: Generate a triangle-by-triangle parametrization using either equal-size or space-optimizing layout.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Builds a trivial triangle-by-triangle parametrization.\
Two methods are provided, the first maps all triangles into equal sized triangles, while the second one adapt the size of the triangles in texture space to their original size.

parameters.label: Quads per line
parameters.help:
Indicates how many triangles have to be put on each line (every quad contains two triangles)
Leave 0 for automatic calculation.

parameters.label: Texture Dimension (px)
parameters.help: Gives an indication on how big the texture is.

parameters.label: Inter-Triangle border (px)
parameters.help: Specifies how many pixels to be left between triangles in parametrization domain.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.help: Choose space optimizing to map smaller faces into smaller triangles in parametrizazion domain.

filters.name: Set Dummy Texture
filters.shortDescription: Give the current mesh a generated checkerboard or grid texture, to show its UV parametrization.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Generates a square test image and makes it the only texture of the current mesh, replacing the textures it had. A checkerboard or a grid makes the scale and distortion of the UV parametrization visible at a glance; the UV grid draws the lines along U in red and those along V in blue, so the two directions can be told apart. The mesh needs texture coordinates, per wedge or per vertex. To use an image of your own, see *Set Texture from File*.

parameters.label: Dummy Texture Size
parameters.help: The side of the dummy texture, which is square, in texels.

parameters.label: Cell Size
parameters.help: Size in pixel of the checkerboard or grid cell of the dummy texture.

parameters.label: Dummy Texture Type
parameters.help: Choose between a checkerboard, a line grid, and a UV grid whose lines along U are red and along V blue.

enumOptions.label: UV Grid
enumOptions.help: Grid lines along U in red and along V in blue, so the two directions can be told apart on the mesh.

filters.name: Set Texture from File
filters.shortDescription: Make an image file the texture of the current mesh, mapped by its UV coordinates.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Loads an image file and makes it the only texture of the current mesh, replacing the textures it had. The mesh needs texture coordinates, per wedge or per vertex. To make a test pattern instead, see *Set Dummy Texture*.

With one texture chosen in **Replace**, only that texture's image is replaced, under the new file's name, and the mesh's other textures and materials stay as they are.

parameters.label: Texture File
parameters.help: The image that becomes the only texture of the mesh.

parameters.label: Replace
parameters.help: The texture whose image the file replaces, or all of them, leaving the file as the only texture.

filters.name: Remove Textures
filters.shortDescription: Detach one texture, or every texture, from the current mesh, keeping its texture coordinates unless asked not to.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Detaches textures from the current mesh -- all of them, or the one chosen in **Texture**. The image files on disk are left alone.

Removing **all** the textures takes the images and the materials that refer to them, so that the mesh is drawn and saved untextured. The texture coordinates stay, so that *Set Dummy Texture* or *Set Texture from File* can give it another texture; **Remove texture coordinates** drops them as well, per wedge and per vertex, when the parametrization itself is not wanted any more.

Removing **one** texture takes that image, and the materials stop using it. A material left with no image at all goes too: the faces that used it become untextured, and every other face keeps the texture it had. A material that keeps another image -- a glTF one losing its normal map, say -- stays, and so do its faces.

parameters.label: Texture
parameters.help: The texture to remove, or all of them.

parameters.label: Remove texture coordinates
parameters.help: Also drop the per-wedge and per-vertex texture coordinates. Only with all the textures, since the others would still use them.

filters.name: Rename Texture
filters.shortDescription: Give one texture of the current mesh a new name, which is the file name it is saved under.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Renames the texture chosen in **Texture**. A texture's name is the file name that saving the mesh writes it under, so this is how a texture made by a filter gets a better file name than the one it was given.

A texture that already has a file is not renamed on disk: that file is left alone, the texture shows as changed in the layer panel, and the next save of the mesh writes it next to the mesh under the new name.

parameters.label: Texture
parameters.help: The texture to rename.

parameters.label: New name
parameters.help: The texture's new name. Without a suffix it is saved as PNG.

filters.name: Transfer Color from Vertex to Texture
filters.shortDescription: Bake per-vertex color into texture image(s) using the current UV parametrization.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Fills the specified texture using per-vertex color data of the mesh.

parameters.label: Texture name
parameters.help: Name of the new texture, which is also its file name when the mesh is saved. Leave it empty to name it after the layer. When the mesh uses more than one texture slot, numeric suffixes are added.

parameters.label: Texture Size
parameters.help: The side of each new texture, which is square, in texels.

parameters.label: Overwrite texture
parameters.help: If current mesh has associated textures, overwrite them instead of creating new files.

parameters.label: Fill texture
parameters.help: If enabled the unmapped texture space is colored using a pull-push filling algorithm, otherwise it is left black.

filters.name: Transfer Texture Color from Another Layer to Vertex
filters.shortDescription: Color the vertices of the current mesh by sampling the texture of a source mesh, at the closest point or along the normal.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Gives each vertex of the current mesh the texture color of the closest point of the **Source Mesh**. The source may be the current mesh itself, to turn its own texture into vertex colors.

parameters.label: Source Mesh
parameters.help: The textured mesh to sample from; it can be the current mesh itself.

parameters.label: Correspondence
parameters.help: How each vertex finds its point on the source.

enumOptions.label: Closest point
enumOptions.help: The point of the source closest to the vertex. Robust, never misses, but bunches samples where the source bends towards the current mesh.

enumOptions.label: Along the normal
enumOptions.help: Where a ray along the vertex normal, either way, meets the source, the outward hit first; the closest point where both rays miss. Samples the source more evenly (Tarini et al. 2003); needs a source with faces.

parameters.label: Max Dist Search
parameters.help: Sample points for which we do not find anything within this distance are rejected and not considered for recovering color.

parameters.label: Source Texture
parameters.help: Choose which associated source texture to sample. Automatic uses the source mesh per-face texture slot assignment.

filters.name: Transfer Vertex Attributes from Another Layer to Texture
filters.shortDescription: Bake vertex color, normals, scalar or the signed distance of a source mesh into a texture of the current mesh, by closest point or along the normal.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
For each texel of the current mesh, finds its point on the surface and the closest point of the **Source Mesh**, and writes there the interpolated vertex attribute chosen in **Data Source**. This may be useful to restore detail lost in simplification. To resample a texture onto another parametrization, use *Transfer Texture from Another Layer*.

*Signed Distance* bakes a displacement map: the distance from each texel's point to the closest point of the source, positive on the side the current mesh's normals point to, into a **16-bit grayscale** texture. 0 marks the texels that found nothing within the search distance, and 1 to 65535 span the distances linearly, from `distance_min` to `distance_max` in the output values, so they can be read back; the texture is not filled around the charts. With a smoothed or simplified copy as the current mesh and the full model as the source, it is the height map of the residual marks of Pietroni et al.: the small relief of the surface, without its shape.

parameters.label: Source Mesh
parameters.help: The mesh whose vertex attributes are transferred.

parameters.label: Data Source
parameters.help: The vertex attribute of the source mesh to write into the texture.

enumOptions.label: Signed Distance
enumOptions.help: The distance to the closest point of the source, signed by the current mesh's normals, as a 16-bit grayscale texture (a displacement map).

parameters.label: Correspondence
parameters.help: How each texel finds its point on the source.

enumOptions.label: Closest point
enumOptions.help: The point of the source closest to the texel's point. Robust, never misses, but bunches samples where the source bends towards the current mesh.

enumOptions.label: Along the normal
enumOptions.help: Where a ray along the current mesh's normal, either way, meets the source, the outward hit first; the closest point where both rays miss. Samples the source more evenly (Tarini et al. 2003), and makes Signed Distance a height along the normal.

parameters.label: Max Dist Search
parameters.help: Sample points for which we do not find anything within this distance are rejected and not considered for recovering data.

parameters.label: Texture name
parameters.help: Name of the new texture, which is also its file name when the mesh is saved. Leave it empty to name it after the layer. When the mesh uses more than one texture slot, numeric suffixes are added.

parameters.label: Texture Size
parameters.help: The side of each new texture, which is square, in texels.

parameters.label: Overwrite Current Texture
parameters.help: If the current mesh has textures, replace their images instead of adding new textures. Their files are left alone.

parameters.label: Fill texture
parameters.help: If enabled the unmapped texture space is colored using a pull-push filling algorithm, otherwise it is left black.

filters.name: Transfer Texture from Another Layer
filters.shortDescription: Resample the texture of a source mesh into a texture of the current mesh, by closest point or along the normal.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: For each texel of the current mesh, finds its point on the surface and the closest point of the **Source Mesh**, and writes there the source's texture color. This re-textures a mesh after remeshing, simplification or a new parametrization: give the new mesh its UVs, make it current, and pick the textured original as the source.

parameters.label: Source Mesh
parameters.help: The textured mesh to sample from.

parameters.label: Source Texture
parameters.help: Which texture of the source mesh to sample. Automatic follows the source's per-face texture assignment.

parameters.label: Correspondence
parameters.help: How each texel finds its point on the source.

enumOptions.label: Closest point
enumOptions.help: The point of the source closest to the texel's point. Robust, never misses, but bunches samples where the source bends towards the current mesh.

enumOptions.label: Along the normal
enumOptions.help: Where a ray along the current mesh's normal, either way, meets the source, the outward hit first; the closest point where both rays miss. Samples the source more evenly (Tarini et al. 2003), and makes Signed Distance a height along the normal.

parameters.label: Max Dist Search
parameters.help: Sample points for which we do not find anything within this distance are rejected and not considered for recovering data.

parameters.label: Texture name
parameters.help: Name of the new texture, which is also its file name when the mesh is saved. Leave it empty to name it after the layer. When the mesh uses more than one texture slot, numeric suffixes are added.

parameters.label: Texture Size
parameters.help: The side of each new texture, which is square, in texels.

parameters.label: Overwrite Current Texture
parameters.help: If the current mesh has textures, replace their images instead of adding new textures. Their files are left alone.

parameters.label: Fill texture
parameters.help: If enabled the unmapped texture space is colored using a pull-push filling algorithm, otherwise it is left black.

filters.name: Convert Object-Space Normal Map to Tangent Space
filters.shortDescription: Convert an object-space normal map into a tangent-space normal map for the current mesh UV slot.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Converts an object-space normal map into a tangent-space normal map using the current mesh geometry, normals, and UV parametrization. The result is suitable for direct use in MeshLab's PBR normal-texture channel.

parameters.label: UV / Material Slot
parameters.help: Choose the mesh texture slot that owns the UV layout to process. Only faces whose per-wedge texture index uses this slot are converted, and this is also the material slot whose PBR normal channel can be updated. This is separate from the source image because the object-space normal map may be stored as another associated texture.

parameters.label: Source Object-Space Normal Map
parameters.help: Choose the associated texture image to interpret as the object-space normal map. Its pixels are sampled through the selected UV / Material Slot.

parameters.label: Target Tangent-Space Normal Map
parameters.help: Where the generated tangent-space normal map goes: over the image of an existing texture, whose file is left alone, or into a new texture added to the mesh, named as given here or after the layer when left empty. Saving the mesh writes it.

parameters.label: Bind As PBR Normal Map
parameters.help: If enabled, the converted texture is added to the mesh associated texture list and assigned to the selected slot's PBR normal channel.

parameters.label: Invert X
parameters.help: Invert the tangent-space X channel in the generated normal map.

parameters.label: Invert Y
parameters.help: Invert the tangent-space Y channel in the generated normal map.

parameters.label: Invert Z
parameters.help: Invert the tangent-space Z channel in the generated normal map.

parameters.label: PBR Normal Scale
parameters.help: Normal intensity stored in the selected material slot when binding the converted map as a PBR normal texture.

filters.name: Pack Texture Images
filters.shortDescription: Combines complete texture images into fewer atlas images and remaps the mesh UVs.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Combines the complete texture images used by the current mesh into a smaller number of atlas images and creates a new mesh layer referencing the result. Each source image is kept intact, placed as a rectangular region in one output image, and copied without rescaling. The mesh's per-wedge texture indices and UV coordinates are then remapped so every triangle continues to sample the same source pixels from their new atlas location. The original mesh and its textures are left unchanged.

This operation packs whole images, not individual UV islands or charts. Use **Defragment Texture Atlas** when the goal is to rearrange or optimize the UV charts themselves. Output image dimensions are determined automatically from the source image sizes and their packed arrangement, so they are not necessarily square or powers of two.

**Target textures** specifies the desired number of output atlas images and must be smaller than the number of texture groups actually used by mesh faces. Source images are distributed between those outputs before rectangular packing.

**Gutter** reserves the requested number of pixels around every source image. Border pixels are extruded into this area, reducing color bleeding when the atlas is displayed with bilinear filtering.

Every face must reference one valid texture consistently across its three wedges, and all UV coordinates must lie inside `[0,1]`. Repeated or tiled texture coordinates cannot be represented safely after whole-image atlas packing, so such meshes are rejected rather than producing altered texture mapping.

parameters.label: Target textures
parameters.help: Number of output images. It must be smaller than the number of texture groups actually used by the mesh.

parameters.label: Gutter (pixels)
parameters.help: Border pixels reserved around every source image. The source image edges are extruded into this area to prevent bilinear-filtering bleed.
